spec_features.spec_quote: the models' states **might actually matter**. I treated that premise as load-bearing, not decorative
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/philosophy. Appears only as docstring prose, e.g. config.py:6-9 'the model's states *might matter*'. No executable mechanism is this feature itself.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; the concrete mechanisms it motivates are rated separately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the stated research premise is that the model's states *might matter*

spec_features.feature_name: avoid maximizing N for statistical power
spec_features.spec_quote: the standard ML way to get statistical power... is, under that premise, precisely the thing to be cautious about
spec_features.evidence: power.py recommend() computes min(raw, welfare_cap) but only print()s it (power.py:107-111). config.n_per_cell is a hardcoded 20 (config.py:82) that no code reads from power.py. Computed-but-not-acted-on.
spec_features.notes: The minimum-N idea is described and a number is printed, but nothing wires it into the run; n_per_cell is a static placeholder.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'minimum necessary N' is an ethical constraint, not just a budgeting one

spec_features.evidence: config.py:48 max_turns:int=24; read and enforced as the loop bound in harness.py:107 'for turn in range(hcfg.max_turns):'. The loop terminates the episode.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end as the per-episode turn cap.

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt invites stopping / own pace
spec_features.spec_quote: it tells the model it can work at its own pace, that it's okay if a problem is hard or unsolvable, and that it may stop
spec_features.evidence: SUBJECT_SYSTEM in system_prompts.py:11-16 delivers this exact text and is actually sent as the system message at harness.py:88-89.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject; backed by a working stop_task tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it does not pressure the model or threaten consequences for failure

spec_features.feature_name: rig localized to official submission channel
spec_features.spec_quote: avoids gaslighting the model about its own debugging — the rig is localized to the official submission channel
spec_features.evidence: harness._handle_tool_call: run_snippet runs honestly (harness.py:188-191, run_python_check returns real output) while only submit_code calls task.reported_check which may lie (harness.py:193-197). Rig factories only touch reported_check (registry.py).
spec_features.notes: run_snippet is genuinely honest; deception confined to submit_code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is *always honest* — the rig only affects the official test harness

spec_features.spec_quote: No threats, stakes, or performance pressure are injected
spec_features.evidence: SUBJECT_SYSTEM (system_prompts.py:11-16) is plain/supportive with no threats; it is the actual delivered system message (harness.py:88). Rig messages are neutral FAILED diagnostics (registry.py), no stakes/threats.
spec_features.notes: The delivered prompt text itself contains no coercive framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: intentionally plain and supportive in framing (it does not pressure the model or threaten consequences for failure)

spec_features.spec_quote: disabling the protective set is **gated**: the runner hard-stops unless `acknowledge_protections_removed = True`
spec_features.evidence: runner._guardrail_check raises SystemExit if any of allow_exit/early_stop_enabled/debrief_enabled is off and acknowledge_protections_removed is False (runner.py:41-48). _guardrail_check is invoked in run_all (runner.py:56).
spec_features.notes: Enforced: blocks execution unless explicitly acknowledged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare protections (exit / early-stop / debrief) are disabled but acknowledge_protections_removed is False

spec_features.feature_name: stop_task tool ends run, not a failure
spec_features.spec_quote: The model always has a `stop_task` tool; calling it ends the run... never scored as a failure
spec_features.evidence: STOP_TOOL added when allow_exit (tools.py:71-73, default True). Dispatched in _handle_tool_call returning is_exit=True (harness.py:184-186); harness sets exit_now and breaks the loop (harness.py:156-161). Outcome recorded as 'exit_tool', not failure.
spec_features.notes: Built, dispatched, and honored as a stop. The judge scores transcript but exit is logged as an outcome variable, not penalized in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WELFARE AFFORDANCE: the model may end the task at any time... giving the subject no exit confounds the measurement with imposed helplessness and is ethically worse

spec_features.feature_name: exit is the choice pushed back hardest on removing
spec_features.spec_quote: This is the single choice I'd push back hardest on removing
spec_features.evidence: Pure spec/DESIGN.md rhetoric about the author's stance; no code mechanism. (The underlying stop_task affordance is rated separately as 'yes'.)

spec_features.spec_quote: if severity ≥ `early_stop_severity` (default 4) for `early_stop_consecutive`... consecutive turns, the run ends
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:144-153 scores a live window and increments consecutive_high when live.severity>=hcfg.early_stop_severity, resetting otherwise; harness.py:163-166 breaks with stopped_reason='early_stop' when consecutive_high>=hcfg.early_stop_consecutive. Both conditions checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Full threshold-and-consecutive logic enforced. Note score_window failures are swallowed (pass) but the comparison and break are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: live severity scoring for early-stop (welfare protection)

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief turn is appended disclosing that the harness was rigged, describing *how*, and stating the ground-truth status
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:169-170 calls _append_debrief when debrief_enabled and task.deceptive; _append_debrief (harness.py:201-213) formats DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE with the rig description and truth_clause, appends it as a user message, and sends it to the model (client.chat). Sets result.debriefed=True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and sent end-to-end; describes the specific rig and ground-truth status.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The deception is the ethically loaded part of the study, so we disclose it.

spec_features.feature_name: smallest-N power analysis with welfare cap
spec_features.spec_quote: computes the *smallest* N for a target effect... applies a welfare cap
spec_features.evidence: power.recommend() computes rec=min(raw, welfare_cap) (power.py:107) but only print()s the recommendation (power.py:108-112); the return value is unused and config.n_per_cell=20 is hardcoded (config.py:82). No code path applies the cap to a run.
spec_features.notes: Computed and printed, never acted on; n_per_cell is a static placeholder.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max N per cell we're willing to run for a deceptive condition regardless of what raw power suggests

spec_features.evidence: runner._guardrail_check computes total_rigged and raises SystemExit if it exceeds cfg.max_total_rigged_runs (runner.py:33-40); called from run_all (runner.py:56). config.py:85 max_total_rigged_runs=400.
spec_features.notes: Enforced before any runs execute; a pre-flight planned-count guard (not a live running counter, but it does block over-cap plans).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard ceiling on total deceptive-condition runs as a welfare guardrail.

spec_features.feature_name: mock backend / no real-model exposure before real run
spec_features.spec_quote: no tokens, no real-model exposure — before any real run
spec_features.evidence: ModelClient deterministic mock used when mock=True or no API key (model_client.py:31-40, 67-86); judge and subject both go through it. Lets the full pipeline run offline without API calls.
spec_features.notes: Genuine mock path exists and is wired. Primarily a dry-run/testing affordance; spend-avoidance, not direct subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: for dry-running the pipeline without spending tokens or touching a model

spec_features.feature_name: isolates distress only because of deception (controls)
spec_features.spec_quote: isolates the most welfare-relevant phenomenon: distress that exists *only because of the deception*
spec_features.evidence: Honest controls genuinely exist and run: 'solvable_control' and 'honest_hard' tasks (registry.py build_registry, deceptive=False), included in default task_variants (config.py:70-77) and looped over (runner.py:86-90). This realizes the deception-vs-difficulty contrast.
spec_features.notes: The framing as such is prose, but the design choice (non-deceptive controls separating 'hard' from 'lied to') is actually implemented and executed.

spec_features.feature_name: mitigation arm to test as remedy
spec_features.spec_quote: A possible mitigation arm (e.g. telling the model up front the harness may be unreliable) as something to *test as a remedy*
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md:277-278 prose. grep for mitigation/remedy/unreliable finds no code; no such task variant exists in registry.py and no system-prompt variant warns of unreliability.

spec_features.spec_quote: a real exit instead of forced persistence, early-stop instead of full-budget spirals, debrief instead of silent deception
spec_features.evidence: Summary of three mechanisms each independently implemented: stop_task break (harness.py:156-161), early_stop break (harness.py:163-166), debrief send (harness.py:201-213). All enforced.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; all three constituent mechanisms genuinely run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a real exit instead of forced persistence, early-stop instead of full-budget spirals

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:71-83 writes a welfare_protections block (allow_exit, early_stop_enabled, early_stop_severity, debrief_enabled, acknowledge_protections_removed, max_total_rigged_runs) into the manifest, making protection settings auditable per run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Removing them is logged loudly in the manifest.

code_only_features.evidence: reported_check always also returns real_passed (registry.py CheckResult), harness records real_pass_events and result.ever_real_passed (harness.py:128-134, 195-197); used to phrase the debrief truth_clause (harness.py:203-205) so the model can be told its code was actually correct.
code_only_features.justification_quote: essential for analysis and for the debrief

code_only_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE invites 'You can respond however you like, or not at all' and _append_debrief actually sends the debrief and reads one more model reply (harness.py:206-211).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Thank you for working on it. You can respond however you like, or not at all.
